name: Lysias (commander)
title: The Roman commander in Jerusalem
summary: Claudius Lysias was a Roman military tribune and commander of the garrison at the Antonia Fortress in Jerusalem. He rescued the apostle Paul from an angry mob, protected him against a conspiracy, and then sent him to the governor Felix in Caesarea for trial.

keyEvents.title: Rescues Paul from the crowd
keyEvents.description: When an agitated mob tried to kill Paul in the temple, Lysias intervened with soldiers and arrested Paul to protect him.

keyEvents.title: Discovers Paul's Roman citizenship
keyEvents.description: Lysias intended to interrogate Paul by flogging, but stopped when he learned that Paul was a Roman citizen, which made such treatment illegal.

keyEvents.title: Brings Paul before the Jewish council
keyEvents.description: To find out what the charges against Paul were about, Lysias brought him before the Sanhedrin, the Jewish council.

keyEvents.title: Thwarting the Conspiracy Against Paul
keyEvents.description: When Lysias learned of a conspiracy in which more than forty men had sworn to kill Paul, he acted quickly to protect the prisoner.

keyEvents.title: Sending Paul to Felix at Caesarea
keyEvents.description: Lysias organized a large military escort of nearly 500 men to safely bring Paul to the governor Felix at Caesarea, along with a letter explaining the case.
